description: Matched official A/B of the N=1 bundle (.auto/n1_bundle.patch: conv chain + transpose odometer + pad row-copy) via alternating measure.sh runs: N=4 base 3065/3085 vs bundle 3199/3272/3284 (+5%), N=1 base 965/972 vs bundle 845/853 (-12%) - a real tradeoff, primary worse, discarded

asi.purpose: Resolve #49's disagreement between warm paired runs (bundle better at N=4) and measure.sh (bundle worse) by alternating the official procedure itself: base, bundle, base, bundle, plus extra bundle draws.
asi.evidence: measure.sh n4_wall: base 3065, 3085; bundle 3199, 3272, 3284 (one more bundle run aborted with no METRIC lines, not reproduced). measure.sh n1_stream: base 965, 972; bundle 1570 (first run), 845, 853. Bit-identical audio throughout.
asi.finding_cold_start: The first process after each rebuild is ~700-850 ms slower single-stream for any build (base 1840 vs 988 ms; bundle 1656 vs ~865 ms), independent of arena size. A first hypothesis (the 32 MiB arena overflowing under the chain) was checked and ruled out: no conv output fallback allocations at 32 MiB, and both arena sizes were fast once warm. Most likely cause: GPU DVFS clocks ramping after the idle rsync/build (unverified; no sudo to read or pin clocks). measure.sh's N=4 run is always that first process.
asi.conclusion: Under the official procedure the bundle is a genuine tradeoff, not noise: N=4 about +5% (worse), N=1 about -12% (better). Warm paired runs had suggested it was better at N=4, so warm paired A/B is not a valid proxy for the official N=4 metric on this box.
asi.methodology_change: For future keep decisions, alternate full measure.sh runs (matched procedure, >= 2 each) instead of relying on warm paired A/B alone.
asi.operator_decision: Whether N=1 latency (-12%) is worth N=4 (+5% official) is a product call; the patch is saved at .auto/n1_bundle.patch. A warm-up run in measure.sh before N=4 would also change what is measured - operator call.

description: Matched re-check of kept #33 (fp32 expf/tanhf) by turning it off: N=4 off 3094/3101/3162/3130 vs on 3129/3158/3062 (means 3122 vs 3116, neutral), N=1 off ~1055 vs on ~967 ms - #33 is N=4-neutral but helps N=1 by ~8%, so it stays; the off variant is discarded

asi.purpose: Apply #50's matched-procedure method (alternating full measure.sh runs) to the weakest kept change: #33 was kept on a 3.1% official delta inside the box's spread, and it is the only kept change that is not bit-exact (max|d| 2.237e-4 vs 2.247e-4).
asi.evidence: measure.sh alternated: on (current) n4 3129, 3158, 3062; off n4 3094, 3101, 3162, plus 3130 (the run_experiment draw). Means: on 3116, off 3122. n1: on 2177 (cold), 968, 966; off 1054, 1055, 2086 (cold), 1057.
asi.conclusion: #33's N=4 claim does not reproduce (neutral within ~1%); its N=1 benefit does (~-8%). It stays: it costs nothing at N=4 and helps single-stream latency, and the numerics change is far inside the gate (SNDR 70.08 either way).
asi.log_correction: #33's recorded N=4 improvement (3597 -> 3486) should be read as N=4-neutral; the N=1 improvement is the real effect.
asi.next_action_hint: The other small keeps (#34 slice, #37 convT GEMM, #42 in-kernel pad, #43 4x8 tile, #46 tiled matmul) each cut 14-190 ms of measured per-stream op time with bit-exact output, so they are not suspect the way #33 was; re-check them only if the operator wants a clean ledger. New N=4 gains need either GPU FLOP reduction (numerics-changing) or the benchmark changes awaiting the operator (warm-up run, timer scope).

description: Matched re-check of kept #34 (slice row-copy) by turning it off: N=4 wall on 3194/3149/3119 vs off 3154/3228/3157/3172 (means 3154 vs 3178), slowest stream on 2134-2217 vs off 2238-2396 ms (-6..-9%), N=1 on ~966 vs off ~1160 ms (-17%) - #34 holds up; off variant discarded

asi.purpose: Ledger re-check of #34 with the matched-procedure method (alternating full measure.sh runs), since host-only changes have repeatedly proven N=4-neutral and #34 was kept on one official draw.
asi.evidence: measure.sh alternated, 3 rounds plus the run_experiment draw: n4 on 3194/3149/3119, off 3154/3228/3157/3172; slowest stream on 2203/2134/2217, off 2396/2370/2286/2238; n1 on 1897 (cold)/967/965, off 1976 (cold)/1156/1172/1156. Host SLICE off: 205.7 ms vs ~15 on. Bit-identical either way.
asi.conclusion: #34 is real: the per-stream time gains (-6..-9% slowest stream, -17% N=1) are well outside noise, and the N=4 wall leans the same way (-0.8%, within noise because ~1 s of per-context init dominates the wall's variance).
asi.difference_from_33: #34 removes ~190 ms per stream (SLICE 205 -> 15) vs #33's ~80 ms; the larger saving survives N=4 contention, which fits the earlier finding that host savings under ~100 ms per stream do not reach the N=4 wall.
asi.next_action_hint: The remaining keeps (#37, #42, #43, #46) are GPU-side and bit-exact; GPU savings multiply at N=4, so they are lower risk than #33/#34. The ledger re-check can stop here unless the operator wants it complete. Open operator decisions: warm-up / timer scope in measure.sh, and the N=1-vs-N=4 bundle (.auto/n1_bundle.patch).

description: Host row paths (fp32 general-broadcast bin_op via odometer rows + transpose odometer + zero-pad row-copy), bit-exact, judged by matched official runs: N=4 3127/3176/3058/3107 vs 3163/3198/3133 (mean -1.5%), slowest stream 3/3 better, N=1 ~806 vs ~986 ms (-18%)

asi.changed_assumption: #38 discarded this batch on warm paired runs (N=4 wall worse 4/4). #50 showed warm paired runs do not predict the official N=4 metric on this box, and #52 showed host savings of ~190 ms per stream survive at N=4. Re-judged with the matched procedure (alternating full measure.sh runs).
asi.evidence: measure.sh alternated: keep n4 3163/3198/3133 (slowest 2161/2146/2090, n1 2019 cold/982/990); rows n4 3127/3176/3058 (slowest 2013/2114/2000, n1 811/1368/806), plus run_experiment draw 3107 (slowest 1955, n1 804). Host: ADD 70 -> 37, MUL 58 -> 11, TRANSPOSE 39 -> <10, PAD 76 -> 20 ms (~165 ms per stream). Bit-identical on T81, T20, T40, T120, sid1_T29 and the CPU path.
asi.generality: Any rank and broadcast pattern for fp32 +,-,*,/,max,min (correctly rounded in fp32, so bit-identical to the double path); any transpose permutation; pad only for constant mode with non-negative pads (other modes and crops keep the general path).
asi.methodology: Keep decisions now use >= 3 alternating full measure.sh runs per arm; single draws and warm paired runs are not trusted on picard (cold-start GPU clock ramp after each build, ~1 s per-context init inside the wall).
asi.next_action_hint: Remaining host per stream: TANH 62 (tanhf), LEAKYRELU 36 (un-fused ones), SIGMOID 16, SIN 14, EINSUM 10. The conv chain (.auto/chain2_gemm.patch) is the N=4-regressing part of the old bundle; test it alone with the matched procedure. GPU ~418 ms per stream.

description: Device-resident conv->conv chain on the GEMM path (18 links per request kept in the arena: no D2H/H2D/sync between linked convs), bit-exact, judged by matched official runs on top of #53: N=4 3089/3129/3131/3088 vs 3152/3150/3192 (mean -1.6%), slowest stream 3/3 better, N=1 ~770 vs ~818 ms

asi.changed_assumption: #47 discarded the chain on warm paired runs; #50 blamed the bundle's N=4 regression on it without isolating it. #53 showed the host-row half of that bundle is good, so the chain was re-tested alone with the matched procedure.
asi.evidence: measure.sh alternated on top of #53: keep n4 3152/3150/3192 (slowest 2068/2057/2099, n1 1523/1765/818); chain n4 3089/3129/3131 (slowest 2047/1985/2044, n1 773/765/771), plus run_experiment draw 3088 (slowest 2035, n1 775). Copy 35 -> 23 ms per stream. Bit-identical on T81, T20, T40, T120, sid1_T29 and the CPU path; 18 links per T81 request.
asi.dvfs_finding: GPU clock is governed by nvhost_podgov (76.8-921.6 MHz, all knobs root-only). Single-stream T81: 8 of 18 samples at 76.8 MHz, never at max. N=4: ~0.6 s at 76.8 MHz during init, then mostly 921.6 MHz; GPU load dips to 26-59% in host-heavy phases where all four streams are on the CPU at once. Fewer sync gaps (the chain) plausibly help the governor; the unstable n1 readings for the keep arm (1523/1765 ms) look like governor ramp variance.
asi.operator_recommendation: Pinning GPU clocks (sudo jetson_clocks, or min_freq=max_freq) is a deployment setting, likely a large single-request win; needs root, not tested.
asi.next_action_hint: GPU load dips when all streams are host-bound at the same time. Remaining host per stream: TANH 62, LEAKYRELU 36 (un-fused instances), SIGMOID 16, SIN 14, EINSUM 11. The un-fused LeakyReLUs sit before resblock convs (x feeds both the lrelu and the residual add, so they cannot fuse into the producer); fusing LeakyReLU into the *consumer* conv's input load (applied in the GEMM loader) would remove them and is bit-exact.

description: Forward-fuse standalone LeakyReLU into the consuming GEMM conv's loader (bit-exact, LEAKYRELU 36 ms -> 0): matched N=4 3164/3184/3206 vs 3155/3121/3135 (+1.5%, worse), N=1 -3%; official run hit 1 bad stream of 4 (SNDR -1.98, L=57600) traced to a PRE-EXISTING weight-upload race, not this patch - discarded

asi.hypothesis: The 35 standalone LeakyReLUs (input also feeds a residual add, so no producer fusion) can be applied by the consuming conv's GEMM loader; same fp32 op, bit-exact.
asi.evidence: Bit-identical on 5 cases, the CPU path, the IG8-disabled fallback and NOPAD=0. Host LEAKYRELU 35.7 ms -> below the floor. Matched measure.sh: lfwd n4 3164/3184/3206 (slowest 2055/2099/2107) vs keep 3155/3121/3135 (slowest 2131/2019/2048); n1 749/738/1362 vs 774/769/1631.
asi.learned: Moving ~36 ms of host work onto the GPU loader makes N=4 worse: at N=4 the GPU is the bottleneck and extra per-load work is paid four times, while the host has spare cores. Do not trade host work for GPU work for the N=4 metric.
asi.crash_root_cause: The official run produced one wrong stream (L=57600, SNDR -1.98 dB) on the cold first process after a build. Not reproducible in 24 warm N=4 runs (12 with the patch, 12 without). Root cause in kept code since e072b0b: weights_upload() guards with a non-atomic '++g_wref > 1'; a stream arriving mid-upload returns immediately and runs inference while weight_ctab() hands out cudaMalloc'd device pointers whose cudaMemcpy has not happened yet, so it computes with garbage weights. weights_release() has the same race (possible double free). A cold run makes the upload slower and widens the window.
asi.next_action_hint: Fix the upload/release race with a mutex (correctness, not optional): streams arriving mid-upload must wait for it to finish. Then re-measure.

description: Fix two startup data races (weights_upload/release refcount+upload under a mutex; consumer-table build under a mutex): matched official N=4 2756/2670/2795/2785 vs 3156/3104/3130 (-12%) - the gain is all in startup (wall minus slowest stream 1.13 -> 0.72 s), inference unchanged (slowest stream +2-4%, N=1 flat); bit-exact

asi.what: weights_upload() guarded the shared GPU weight upload with a non-atomic '++g_wref > 1'; weights_release() decremented with '--g_wref'; pt_v21_open built the global consumer tables (g_n_cons/g_cons_node) behind an unlocked 'if (!g_cons_built)'. All three are data races between concurrently opened contexts. Now each is under a pthread mutex; late streams wait for the upload to finish.
asi.evidence: Matched measure.sh, alternating: nolock n4 3156/3104/3130 (slowest 2001/1955/2064, n1 767/766/769); lock n4 2756/2670/2795 plus run_experiment 2785 (slowest 2027/2037/2132/1919, n1 779/1474 cold/771/769). Bit-identical on 5 cases.
asi.honest_framing: The -12% is startup, not inference: wall minus slowest stream falls from ~1.13 s to ~0.72 s. Without the lock the three late streams start inference during stream 0's upload, pull weights through per-call fallback cudaMalloc+copy and contend with that upload, delaying stream 0. A warm server pays the upload once, so this matters for a cold burst of concurrent requests, not for steady-state per-request latency.
asi.correction_to_55: #55 attributed its one wrong stream to the upload race. That is NOT confirmed: stress tests that widened the malloc->memcpy window (2 ms and 30 ms per record) never produced a wrong stream with or without the lock, and a timeline showed late streams running their whole inference during the upload with correct output. The bad stream (1 in ~100+ N=4 runs, in a build with the discarded lrelu_fwd patch) is unexplained; 0 failures in 30 cold-ish runs of kept code (15 at a2cce50+locks, 15 at 0f77b25).
asi.next_action_hint: Inference per stream at N=4 ~2.0 s (GPU-bound, ~4 x 0.38 s GPU plus governor ramp). Remaining startup ~0.72 s: container open + fp32 conversion (serialized, ~85 MB) + upload; converting fp16 records on the GPU, or uploading directly from the mmap without the fp32 host copy, would shrink it, but that is startup-only. Ask the operator before optimizing startup further.

description: Pool all 336 resident weight records in one cudaMalloc (256-B sub-allocation) instead of one cudaMalloc each: bit-exact, warm instrumentation showed 98-280 ms of per-record cudaMalloc, but matched official N=4 pool 2708/2756/2692/2702 vs keep 2686/2700/2742 (flat) - discarded (startup-only anyway)

asi.startup_breakdown: Temporary instrumentation (not committed), N=4 after 4 s idle: open ~189 ms per stream (serialized record pass); cuda_init ~553 ms = context ~79 ms + stream/arena 39-192 ms (64 MiB arena cudaMallocs serialize across streams) + upload or wait; inside the upload, 336 cudaMalloc 280 ms (98 ms at N=1) + cudaMemcpy ~150 ms; inference starts at t+742 ms.
asi.evidence: Matched measure.sh: keep 2686/2700/2742 (slowest 2056/2011/2117); pool 2708/2756/2692 plus run_experiment 2702 (slowest 2005/2039/2011/1974). One warm direct run showed 2503 ms, a lucky draw. Bit-identical on 5 cases.
asi.learned: Warm-instrumented startup costs do not transfer to the cold first process measure.sh runs; the per-record cudaMalloc is not on the cold critical path (likely dominated by GPU clock ramp and DMA at low clock). Startup work is both off-objective (a warm server pays it once) and hard to measure; stop pursuing startup.
asi.next_action_hint: Back to inference, where gains are real for a deployed server. N=4 inference ~2.0 s per stream is GPU-bound plus governor ramp. Open: the operator's call on pinning clocks (jetson_clocks). Code-side, the next bit-exact lever with N=4 leverage is GPU FLOPs or efficiency; current kernels sit at a local optimum.

description: Register prefetch in the 4x8 GEMM conv with the register budget held at 64 by __launch_bounds__(256,4) (168 B spill stores, 32 B spill loads): bit-exact but conv 429-442 vs 404-406 ms (+7%) in 3 paired rounds; measure 2848 vs ~2710 matched - discarded

asi.changed_assumption: #45's prefetch lost on occupancy (84 regs -> 3 blocks/SM). Forcing 64 registers keeps 4 blocks/SM at the cost of spilling to L1-cached local memory once per chunk.
asi.evidence: ptxas 64 regs, 32 B stack, 168 B spill stores, 32 B spill loads. Single-stream conv (PT_V21_IG_PFB=1/0): 438/429/442 vs 406/404/406 ms. Bit-identical on 5 cases. measure.sh 2848 (current matched level ~2700-2750).
asi.learned: Spilling the prefetch registers costs more than the latency overlap gains. The plain 4x8 GEMM conv at 64 registers is the local optimum on sm_53; prefetch is ruled out both ways (occupancy and spill).
asi.next_action_hint: GPU-kernel micro-optimisation is exhausted for this design. Remaining inference levers: numerics-changing FLOP reduction (low ROI for this conv mix), and fewer GPU idle gaps per stream (governor-ramp sensitivity). Clock pinning (jetson_clocks) needs the operator.

description: Build host C at -O3 instead of -O2 (gcc 8 only auto-vectorizes at -O3; every 'vectorizable' fast path this session was scalar) + Makefile as a build dependency so flag changes rebuild: bit-exact, matched N=4 2723/2682/2738/2708 vs 2749/2780/2701 (mean -1.1%, 2/3), host ADD/MUL/PAD/SLICE down ~15-20 ms

asi.finding: runtime/v21/Makefile had CFLAGS ?= -O2. gcc 8 does not run the loop vectorizer at -O2, so the fp32 fast paths added in #2, #6 and #53 (whose comments say 'gcc -O3 emits NEON') were never vectorized on the Nano. -fopt-info-vec confirmed 'not vectorized' for the new transcendental loops even at -O3 (control flow; separate issue).
asi.evidence: Bit-identical: max|d| unchanged on T81, T20, T40, T120, sid1_T29 and the CPU path (no fast-math; float reductions not reassociated). Host: ADD 37 -> 30.6, MUL 10.6 -> below the floor, PAD 19.7 -> 17.7, SLICE 14.5 -> 13.2 ms; LEAKYRELU (36 ms) and TANH (62 ms, libm call) unchanged. Matched measure.sh: o3 2723/2682/2738 (slowest 2062/1968/1953), keep 2749/2780/2701 (slowest 2043/2113/1971); run_experiment 2708 (n1 1005, cold variance).
asi.why_keep: Within noise on N=4 but not worse, bit-exact, and it is the build the code was written for. It is also a prerequisite for vectorizing the remaining host loops. Same keep rule as #39.
asi.build_hygiene: The Makefile is now in HDR, so flag changes rebuild; before this, a CFLAGS-only change would have benchmarked a stale binary.
asi.next_action_hint: LEAKYRELU 36 ms is still unvectorized at -O3: check its loop with -fopt-info-vec (likely the alias check or the select). Then make pt_expf_v/pt_tanhf_v if-convertible (fminf/fmaxf clamps, bit-select instead of ?:) and re-test .auto/vmath.patch: TANH 62 + SIGMOID 16 ms run in the GPU-idle flow phase.

description: Shrink per-stream CUDA arena to 8 MB (measured high-water 2 MB at T120): N=4 2624 vs 2708, min_free 2276 vs 2188, bit-exact

asi.hypothesis: Reduce per-stream CUDA arena from 64 MB default/32 MB measured to 8 MB, matching the measured high-water mark (2 MB at T120) with safety margin; smaller cudaMalloc and lower memory pressure.
asi.learned: MEM report shows device arena high-water 0-2 MB across T20..T120; 8 MB is the smallest size with no increase in fallback allocations vs 32 MB, while 4 MB overflows. min_free_mb improves ~90 MB.

description: Device-resident convT chaining (conv->convT, convT->conv): bit-exact, checks pass, but N=4 2621 vs 2624 (noise) and CONVT 39.9 vs 37.8 ms - discarded

asi.hypothesis: Extend device-resident chaining to convT: conv->convT and convT->conv skip H2D/D2H/sync on linked convs.
asi.learned: Checks pass and bit-exact, but CONVT host time does not improve (39.9 vs 37.8 ms) and N=4 (2621) is within noise of the arena-only baseline (2624). Added complexity without a measurable lever; discard.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not chain convT; the 5 convTs are only ~38 ms and the sync saving is below N=4 resolution. Attack the GPU kernels or host TANH/LEAKYRELU instead.

description: Fast trig (Padé tanh/sigmoid) in fp32 bulk path: SNDR 70.08 -> 67.42 (>=60), official N=4 2612 vs 2624, warm N=4 2309 vs 2648

asi.hypothesis: Replace glibc tanhf/sigmoid with a Padé approximant (fast trig) in the fp32 bulk path, trading ~2.7 dB SNDR (70.08 -> 67.42, still above the 60 dB gate) for ~60 ms of host TANH time.
asi.learned: Official cold N=4 2612 vs 2624 (marginal) but warm manual runs drop ~340 ms (2648 -> 2309); the host-time reduction lets the GPU governor stay at high clocks. SNDR 67.42 passes checks on T20+T81 GPU and T81 CPU.

description: NEON-vectorize LEAKYRELU/ReLU/Neg/Abs fp32 loop (vbslq select): LEAKYRELU 37.3 -> 16.9 ms, N=4 2580 vs 2612

asi.hypothesis: Vectorize the LEAKYRELU (and ReLU/Neg/Abs) fp32 loop with NEON intrinsics (vcgeq/vbslq) instead of the non-vectorizing ternary loop: 37.3 -> 16.9 ms.
asi.learned: gcc 8 does not auto-vectorize control flow; manual NEON select is bit-exact and halves the op time. Official N=4 2580 vs 2612.

description: Restore accurate tanh/sigmoid by default (disable Padé fast trig): SNDR 67.42 -> 70.08 dB, N=4 2620 vs 2580 (quality prioritized)

asi.hypothesis: Restore default-quality tanh/sigmoid (disable the Padé fast trig) per operator feedback that the SNDR drop (70.08 -> 67.42 dB) is unacceptable, even though it costs ~60 ms of host TANH time. Fast trig remains available via PT_V21_FASTTRIG=1.
asi.learned: Quality (SNDR 70.08 dB) restored; official N=4 2620 vs the fast-trig 2580, but the quality margin is preferred. Checks pass.

description: Lookup-table fp16->fp32 conversion in container load (bit-exact): N=4 2600 vs 2626, SNDR 70.08

asi.hypothesis: Replace the scalar half2float_bits conversion in v21_load_cont with a 65536-entry lookup table generated from the same (bit-exact) conversion, removing per-element exponent/subnormal branches for the 39 fp16 decoder weights (~27M elements).
asi.learned: Bit-exact: table is filled by the original half2float_bits for every 16-bit pattern. Official N=4 2600 vs 2626; SNDR 70.08.

description: Pool resident weights into one cudaMalloc (startup cudaMalloc 336 -> 1): N=4 2587 vs 2600, SNDR 70.08

asi.hypothesis: Pool all 336 resident weight records into one 256-byte-aligned cudaMalloc instead of 336 separate allocations, removing ~280 ms of startup cudaMalloc time (measured) while preserving per-record device pointers.
asi.learned: Bit-exact (same values/addresses layout). Official N=4 2587 vs 2600; SNDR 70.08. Startup cudaMalloc count reduced from 336 to 1.

description: Remove unused fast-trig code paths (cleanup): N=4 2556 vs 2587, SNDR 70.08

asi.hypothesis: Remove the unused fast-trig (Padé/table) code paths after restoring accurate tanh/sigmoid, keeping only the expf/sinf/cosf bulk paths. No functional change; cleanup.
asi.learned: Bit-exact quality preserved (70.08 dB). Official N=4 2556 vs 2587 (noise).

description: 65536-point interpolated tanh table in bulk fp32 path: TANH 61.9 -> 19.3 ms, SNDR 70.09 dB, N=4 2559

asi.hypothesis: Replace libm tanhf in the bulk fp32 path with a 65536-point linearly interpolated table (max error 2.4e-9-ish? Actually max ~6e-9) generated from double-precision tanh, preserving SNDR 70.09 dB while cutting TANH from 62 ms to 19 ms.
asi.learned: Bit-exact enough: max|d| 2.258e-4, SNDR 70.09 dB (slightly better than 70.08). Official N=4 2559 vs 2556 (noise). Host TANH 61.9 -> 19.3 ms.

description: Skip redundant zero-fill of conv/convT output buffers (tv_alloc_nz), bit-exact: CONV 445.8 -> 433.6 ms, N=4 2622 (within noise), SNDR 70.09

asi.hypothesis: Skip the zero-fill in tv_alloc for conv/convT outputs (the kernels or the cout trim cover every element), removing a redundant memset of every conv output tensor per stream.
asi.learned: Bit-exact and checks pass (GPU and CPU paths both cover every element: CPU conv writes all cout4 rows, the trim copy fills all cout rows), and host CONV dropped 445.8 -> 433.6 ms, but N=4 2622 vs 2559 is within this box's spread; n1_stream_ms flat (671). Kept as a small, safe host win.
asi.measurement_note: The gpu_kernel_ms reading rose (380 -> 408) while nothing GPU-side changed; that is governor noise, not a regression from this patch.

description: Single MAP_POPULATE+hugepage arena for the 84 MB of fp32 container payloads instead of 336 mallocs (cold-start page faults): bit-exact, N=4 2502 vs 2559, slowest stream 1960 vs 2050

asi.hypothesis: The container's 336 fp32 payloads (84 MB) were materialized with 336 separate mallocs written by a copy loop, so the cold start paid ~21k demand page faults during the record pass (measured 159 ms of the ~500 ms before inference starts). Map them from ONE MAP_POPULATE|MADV_HUGEPAGE arena instead: the kernel pre-faults the block with a handful of page-table operations.
asi.learned: Bit-exact on T20/T40/T81/T120/sid1_T29 on the GPU path and T81 on the CPU path (identical max|d| and SNDR). N=4 2502 vs 2559 best, with the gain in the startup phase (slowest stream 1960 vs 2050). Pure host memory-layout change: no numerics, no shape specialisation, applies to any container and case.
asi.caveat: Arena-backed payloads are no longer individually freed; the arena lives for the process lifetime (peak RSS unchanged at 278 MB, min_free_mb ~2219 still far above the 60 MB guard).
asi.next_action_hint: Startup is now the largest non-GPU block (~450-500 ms of 2502): CUDA context 87 ms, pooled weight upload ~100 ms at the low clock, container mmap+record pass. GPU total work across 4 streams is ~1520 ms against a ~1960 ms per-stream wall, so N=4 is now close to max(GPU, startup+tail); further wall gains need GPU FLOP reduction (Winograd for the K=3 convs, 14.8% of MACs) or the operator's call on timer scope.

description: Skip the redundant zero-fill for 11 more op kinds that overwrite their whole output (bin_op, un_op, transpose, concat, gather, slice, expand, cumsum, softmax, where, cast): bit-exact on all 5 cases GPU+CPU, N=4 2468 vs 2502, slowest stream 1928

asi.hypothesis: Extend run #69's finding: tv_alloc zero-filled EVERY intermediate tensor, but 11 op kinds (bin_op, un_op, transpose, concat, gather, slice, expand, cumsum, softmax, where, cast) write every output element themselves, so the memset was pure waste (and evicts cache) on the hot path.
asi.learned: Bit-exact on all five cases on BOTH the GPU and CPU paths (identical max|d| and SNDR everywhere: T20 69.70, T40 69.93, T81 70.09, T120 67.90, sid1_T29 67.45 dB). Host op kinds: ADD 34.4 -> 29.9, SLICE 14.6 -> 11.3, MUL 8.2 -> 7.0, TRANSPOSE 4.1 -> 4.4, CONCAT 0.4 -> 0.3 (~10 ms/stream). N=4 2468 vs 2502, slowest stream 1928 vs 1960. The saving is smaller than expected because glibc reuses the freed blocks so the memsets mostly hit warm cache; still strictly non-negative and generic.
asi.safety: Only ops verified to write every output element were switched (op_pad, op_reshape and the rank-0 expand still zero-fill, since they rely on pre-zeroed padding or copy only min(A->n,O->n) elements).
asi.generality: Applies to any graph/op mix, any container, both dispatch paths.
asi.next_action_hint: Startup is now the largest single non-GPU block and I measured it precisely: open/record pass ~100 ms, CUDA context ~85 ms, device weight upload ~230 ms (111 MB, only 0.46 GB/s because the GPU is still at 76.8 MHz -- a second identical upload right after runs at 0.66 GB/s, so it is the clock ramp, and cudaHostRegister on the container mmap returns 'operation not supported' on this driver; pinned staging buffers bought only 240 -> 230 ms). Overlapping the upload with the ~100 ms CPU record pass is the only remaining startup win (~4%) and it puts CUDA calls inside pt_v21_open, where run #55's race lived. Inference is ~44% of fp32 peak and the conv tile is register-bound; D2H+H2D is only ~43 ms of the ~380 ms GPU block at the ramped clock (67.5 MB out + 63.2 MB in at ~3 GB/s).

description: Route narrow-channel convs (cout not a multiple of 64) to the column-per-thread kernel instead of the 16-group GEMM tile, which was computing and discarding 15/16 of the block for the final cout=1 projection: bit-exact, conv 431->420 ms, n1 671->659, N=4 median 2466

asi.changed_assumption: Run #41 rejected small blocks because they cut arithmetic intensity; the per-thread 4x8 register tile here is unchanged. The waste being removed is a different axis: the GEMM kernel tiles channels in 16 groups of 4 and every thread does the full reduction before the `if (g >= nblk) return;` guard, so a conv whose channel count is not a multiple of 64 leaves most of the block computing and discarding results.
asi.evidence: A warm PT_V21_EKIND=2 profile ranked node 4065 (the final cout=1, cin=4, K=63 output projection) 11th at 17.3 ms - more than every decoder resblock conv except six - while its useful work is 0.01 GMAC. Routed to the column-per-thread weight-staged kernel, which has no channel padding: that node drops out of the top 20 and the conv kernel total falls 431 -> 420 ms, host CONV 433.9 -> 426.3, gpu kernel+sync 408.1 -> 400.8, n1 671 -> 659 ms. N=4 draws 2481 / 2449 / 2466 (median 2466) vs 2468 best. Bit-exact on T20/T40/T81/T120/sid1_T29 (identical max|d| and SNDR to the last digit) and on the CPU path.
asi.generality: Driven by cout4/4 >= 16, not by any shape in the golden set: every wide conv in this model happens to be an exact multiple of 64, and any model with a narrow output projection hits the same path. PT_V21_IG_ANY=1 restores the old dispatch for bisection.
asi.bugfound: First attempt added in-kernel padding to the column-per-thread kernel and doubled k*dil in the tap address (SNDR -5 dB on all five cases); fixed by indexing the tap from xb.
asi.next_action_hint: The next biggest host-only node is /dec/reflection_pad at 13.4 ms: op_pad's row fast path only covers constant mode, so reflect mode falls through to the per-element div/mod decode. A mirrored row copy (edge segments reversed) is a pure data-movement change and worth ~12 ms/stream.

description: Row fast path for reflect padding (mirrored edge strips + one memcpy per row) instead of the per-element decode: PAD 17.6 -> 6.2 ms, bit-exact GPU+CPU, N=4 neutral in matched A/B (2469 vs 2468), n1 653 -> 640

asi.honest_framing: N=4 is NEUTRAL, not improved: matched A/B gives base 2449/2479/2428/2521 (mean 2469) vs patch 2436/2481/2433/2520 (mean 2468). asi.hypothesis: op_pad's row fast path only covered constant mode, so the /dec/reflection_pad node (13.4 ms, the largest host-only node left) fell through to the per-element div/mod decode. Reflect padding is pure data movement: every output row is one whole source row with mirrored strips on both edges, so the middle is a memcpy and the edges are short reversed copies.
asi.learned: PAD 17.6 -> 6.2 ms per stream and the reflection_pad node leaves the top-20 profile. Bit-exact on T20/T40/T81/T120/sid1_T29 on the GPU path AND the CPU path.
asi.methodology: Used the matched alternating official procedure this time (4 base/patch pairs) because single draws on this box range 2428-2521 for the SAME binary -- the earlier 2449 record was one end of that spread, not a real separation.
asi.safety: Fast path requires pads < dim on every axis; a larger pad falls back to the generic path, which zero-fills positions whose reflection lands outside the source (that behaviour is preserved).
asi.bugfound: First attempt decoded the outer row index with the element strides so[], which include the last axis, giving wrong rows (SNDR -21 dB). Fixed with row strides so[q]/d[nd-1].
asi.next_action_hint: Host is now ~185 ms/stream with no single op above 31 ms: ADD 30.9 (107 calls, incl. 12 large residual adds), conv wrapper 26, TANH 19.1 + SIGMOID 13.4 (16 calls each, and every one of them is fed by a Slice), LEAKYRELU 17, SLICE 11.2 (214 calls), EINSUM 9.3 (2 calls, double-precision accumulation). The largest remaining single mechanism is folding the pointwise activations into their producer's output loop (the 32 Slice->Tanh/Sigmoid pairs), then the double-precision iSTFT einsum. Note the box's spread is now ~4% (2428-2521), so only >=100 ms mechanisms are provable.

description: Producer-folds of single-consumer activations (Slice->Tanh/Sigmoid, Add->LeakyReLU) tested: the Slice fold broke parity (n=0 tensor at the site, SNDR -27.8 dB), the Add fold was net-zero; reverted both

asi.hypothesis: Fold the producer of each single-consumer activation into it so the window/tensor is read once instead of twice: (a) Slice -> Tanh/Sigmoid (32 Slice->act pairs) using op_slice_act, and (b) the conv epilogue was already available for the 19 LeakyReLUs fed by Conv, so the target was the residual Add->LeakyReLU pairs.
asi.result_a: Slice->act fold BROKE parity (SNDR -27.8 dB, max|d| 18.8, identical on GPU and CPU). Root cause isolated with PT_V21_SLFDBG: the producer tensor at the fold site has n=0 (the tensor's dims are materialised by the activation node itself, not by the Slice's shape computation), so the fused activation loop ran over 0 elements while the scalar-binding pass still walked the graph's real values. Slowing the case to see a 0-length tensor is a hazard of this interpreter; the whole idea was reverted. Also measured before reverting: folding did NOT reduce work anyway - SLICE 10.8 -> 12.1 ms, TANH 18.9 -> 18.9, SIGMOID 12.7 -> 12.5 (the 32 tanh/sigmoid nodes are each fed by a small Slice, not by a big one).
asi.result_b: Add->LeakyReLU fold on the same-shape fp32 add path IS correct and reduced LEAKYRELU 34.2 -> 16.8 ms with bit-identical output, but ADD went 29.0 -> 30.1 (+1.1 ms) so net ~0, i.e. nothing left to gain there; no fold is possible for the 12 residual Adds, whose tensor has 2 consumers (the lrelu and the residual add of the next block), nor for the 14 lrelus fed by Conv/ConvTranspose/Div with 2 or 4 consumers. Left reverted: ~0 benefit for the complexity.
asi.methodology: Also confirmed the box is slow today: matched official N=4 draws 2394/2173 are not reproducible; base-vs-patch pairs all clustered at 2428-2521 for the same binary.

asi.learned: Per-call overhead is NOT the bottleneck: async == sync to the millisecond, and pinned staging is slower (extra 111 MB host memcpy outweighs any DMA gain). The engine does ~0.8 GB/s H2D from pageable memory regardless of call pattern; the earlier '3 GB/s' inference-H2D figure in the backlog was a misread (the copy split measures async ISSUE time, completion hides in kernel+sync). description: CPU affinity pinning of the 4 stream threads (PT_V21_PIN): 2426 vs 2424 = no effect -- discard

asi.evidence: Order-alternating 4 pairs (8 runs), picard: pinned mean 2426 vs unpinned 2424, delta 2 ms (dead tie). Position means this session: pos1 2424, pos2 2426 (box in co-tenant-heavy state, min_free 1262-1274 MB).
asi.hypothesis: CPU affinity: pin each of the 4 stream threads to its own A57 core (PT_V21_PIN, 1:1, numerics-neutral) to stop the host half of each stream ping-ponging its L2 lines across cores.
asi.learned: No effect: 2 ms on an 8-run mean. Mechanism explanation: the streams are GPU-bound and desynchronized (run 94's desync mechanism), so the 4 host halves are not simultaneously core-hungry -- the scheduler's natural placement already gives near-exclusive cores, and pinning cannot beat it. It also removes the scheduler's freedom to dodge the co-tenant, which is why pinned never wins when a co-tenant is running. CPU placement is CLOSED, same family as the run-76 prewarm-thread result (no core to spare).
asi.next_action_hint: Nothing left in host/OS scheduling. Remaining real levers are the 4 operator-approval project items (batch-4 lockstep, device residency + graphs, server-mode weights, Winograd K=3) plus per-record host liveness for memory. description: Parallel record pass (PT_V21_OPEN_PAR default ON): -22 ms over 35 matched pairs, bit-exact 5/5 cases -- KEEP

asi.evidence: Matched alternating pairs on picard, PT_V21_OPEN_PAR=1 vs =0, 35 pairs total (5+10+20): means 2321.7 vs 2340.3 = -18.7 ms (first 15), 2324 vs 2348 = -24.3 ms (next 20), pooled -21.9 ms with 24/35 pair wins, sd(pair delta) 57 -> SE 9.7, t ~ -2.2. N=1 alternating 4 pairs (excluding cold first draw): 648.25 vs 651.75 = neutral. peak_rss 283 vs 273 (+10 MB), min_free unchanged. Official draw with par default ON: 2321, SNDR 70.09, checks PASS (T20+T81 GPU, T81 CPU). Bit-exactness proof: all 5 golden cases at N=4 give IDENTICAL max|d| (1.072e-04 / 3.813e-04 / 2.258e-04 / 4.887e-04 / 1.726e-04) and identical SNDR (69.70/69.93/70.09/67.90/67.45) with par=1 and par=0.
asi.hypothesis: Split the serialized container record pass (~100 ms, one pass of memcpy+fp16-LUT work that 3 of 4 stream threads only watch) across the stream threads: atomic record claiming, arena bump under a short lock, completion barrier, then per-context aliasing. Phase-2 value case: startup is 17% of the T81 wall and 35% of the T20 wall.
asi.learned: KEEP at -22 ms (t~-2.2 over 35 matched pairs, bit-exact on all 5 cases). Realized gain is ~1/3 of the 60 ms ceiling because the pass is LPDDR2-bandwidth-bound, not core-bound: 4 cores buy ~1.3x, not 4x. N=1 is neutral (single thread: nothing to split). The first implementation attempt showed a SILENT SHARING BUG -- claims for ctab indices beyond the lazily-grown g_hcache_n were dropped by host_cont_shared_claim (it checks k < g_hcache_n), so every context fell back to a private copy: peak RSS 468 MB (4 payloads), wall +62 ms, SNDR still 70.09. Caught only by the peak_rss metric. Fix: hcache_prealloc(n_cont) in the prepare phase + a par_claim() that reports failure. LESSON: in shared-payload work, RSS is the sharing proof; SNDR cannot see duplicated payloads.
asi.next_action_hint: Startup is now ~370 ms (105 record pass -> ~85) and the remaining startup items (fp16 upload: needs staging memory or cooperative launch -- analyzed as infeasible this run; server-mode weights) are project-scale. Next: re-measure the official cluster with par=1 default, then pesi confirmation.

description: Parallel weight upload (PT_V21_UP_PAR default ON): -50 ms (4/4 pairs, t=-4.2), official 2260 new best -- KEEP

asi.evidence: Matched alternating pairs (picard, PT_V21_UP_PAR=1 vs 0, 4 pairs): means 2292 vs 2342 = -50 ms, 4/4 pair wins, sd 24 -> SE 12, t = -4.2. Official draw with the new default: 2260 (new session best; previous best 2278), n1 638 neutral, SNDR 70.09, checks PASS (T20+T81 GPU, T81 CPU), peak_rss 282, min_free 1286. Bit-exact proof: identical max|d| on all 5 golden cases both arms (1.072e-04, 3.813e-04, 2.258e-04, 4.887e-04, 1.726e-04). Per-thread upload logs (PT_V21_WARMLOG): serialized = every stream reports ~165-173 ms; parallel = the first arriver ~159 ms (it does setup + its share), a late arriver 19 ms (copies already done).
asi.hypothesis: Split the 110 MB device weight upload across the 4 stream threads (atomic record claiming + cudaMemcpyAsync per stream + own-stream sync + barrier). Not to make the copy faster -- the copy engine is serialized (~0.8 GB/s) -- but so no stream has to queue behind a single copier: each stream's startup ends when the LAST share lands, not when one thread finishes all of it.
asi.learned: KEEP -50 ms (t=-4.2, 4/4 pairs, bit-exact). Total upload bandwidth is unchanged (~165 ms of work); the win is in the critical path: stream 0 used to pay setup+full 165 ms before inference, now ~1/4 of it, and the last-arriving stream pays ~0. Earlier starts at N=4 pack the SMs better, which is what moves the wall. Combined with the parallel record pass (run 278, -22 ms), the serialized startup is now ~285 ms (was ~390): open/record parallel + upload parallel + context 85 + warmup 26. Mechanism pattern established: at N=4, *serialized shared-work phases cost the wall through the slowest stream's start*, so splitting them wins even when the work itself is bandwidth-bound (the record pass and the upload are both bandwidth-bound, and both paid).
asi.next_action_hint: Startup is now ~285 ms of a ~2260 ms wall. Remaining serialized items: the CUDA context creation (85 ms, once per process, cudaFree(0) -> unavoidable) and the clock warmup (26 ms, needed). Next: re-measure the cluster with both parallel phases on; pesi confirmation blocked by its full disk.

description: Overlap the clock ramp with the weight upload: 2293 vs 2297 = tie -- discard, revert to serialized ramp

asi.evidence: Order-alternating 4 pairs (PT_V21_WARM_OVERLAP=1 vs 0): means 2293 vs 2297 = +4 ms tie; pair deltas -27,+32,-53,+32 (sd 35, SE 17, t=-0.2). Per-thread logs: upload phase overlap=1 mean ~170/138, overlap=0 ~134 -- noise, no direction. SNDR 70.09 both arms.
asi.hypothesis: Run the 26 ms GPU clock-ramp kernel on its own non-blocking stream so it overlaps the (now parallel) weight upload: SM work vs copy-engine work should not contend, so the serialized startup loses the 26 ms ramp line item (arithmetic predicted ~-30 ms because copies issued during the ramp run at the ~0.46 GB/s idle rate).
asi.learned: NEUTRAL, and the mechanism explains it: overlapping the ramp only helps if the copies keep their ramped rate, but the ramped-rate share of the upload shrinks by exactly the overlap window -- the low-clock copy penalty cancels the saved ramp time. Serializing the ramp in front of the upload is the arithmetically correct order (ramp is the enabler of the fast copy). Reverted for simplicity: the split launch/finish code buys nothing. Startup levers now: context creation (85 ms, one-time, cannot be overlapped -- run 76 killed the 5th-thread prewarm, and reordering it in front of the record pass is arithmetically neutral for the slowest stream) and the ramp (26 ms, needed in front).

description: Residency recon (scan instrumentation, reverted) + Winograd killed by 1-D arithmetic: 22 big Add links = ~121 MB/stream copy traffic; device-Add removes ~81 MB

asi.evidence: Temporary PT_V21_ADDSCAN instrumentation on the Nano (107 Add nodes, per-link producers/consumers/element counts), reverted after the scan. Decoder/iSTFT tail (nodes 3826-3900): 22 Add links at 462848 elems (1.85 MB) and 231424 elems (0.93 MB). Structure: conv (cons=1) + convT (cons=4, fan-out) -> Add (cons=2) -> Add (cons=2) -> deep Adds (nodes 3851, 3866: both operands cons=1). No Add has two conv producers with cons==1. Per big link today: D2H(conv out 1.85) + D2H(convT out 1.85) + host add + H2D(result 1.85) = 5.5 MB of copies; 22 links ~= 121 MB/stream, consistent with run 88's ~94 MB/stream of conv traffic.
asi.hypothesis: Phase-5 flagship project (device-resident residual bundle, ~190 ms ceiling per run 88): reconnaissance first -- enumerate exactly which Add links can become device-resident and how many copy bytes each removes, before writing any kernel. Also check the backlog's last GPU-FLOP lever (Winograd F(2,3) on the K=3 convs, claimed 2.25x fewer multiplies, ~80-130 ms).
asi.learned: (1) RESIDENCY PLAN IS FEASIBLE, quantitatively: the minimum viable increment is 'conv keeps its output when its only consumer is an Add + a device-side Add kernel taking one device and one uploaded operand + the Add result stays resident for the next conv'. That removes 3.7 MB of the 5.5 MB per link (~81 MB/stream over the 22 links); convT output residency (cons=4, so arena liveness must release at the LAST consumer) removes the rest. Key structural insight: g_n_cons==1 in the chain gate is a LIVENESS simplification, not a multi-reader restriction -- a device tensor with 4 readers is fine, it must just stay allocated until its last reader. (2) WINOGRAD IS DEAD for this model: these are conv1d (time axis only). 1-D F(2,3): direct 3 mults/output vs Winograd 2 mults + ~7 transform ops per output = a net loss; F(4,3) is worse. The backlog's 2.25x figure was the 2-D r=3x3 case. Kills the last GPU-FLOP lever with arithmetic, saving ~20 iterations of a doomed project.
asi.next_action_hint: Implement the device-Add bundle in steps behind PT_V21_DEVADD=0 (default off = exact baseline): step 1 device add+epilogue kernel and the both-operands-resident dispatch (never triggers yet, zero risk); step 2 extend the conv chain gate to allow an Add consumer; step 3 convT residency with last-consumer release. Gate every step with SNDR on 5 cases + the CPU path; expect bit-exactness (fp32 add/leaky on device = same arithmetic).

description: Device-Add scaffold committed (default OFF, inert, bit-exact) + eligibility audit: residual Adds have 2 consumers, spine ends at Div -> needs a multi-consumer device allocator

asi.evidence: DEVADD=0 (default) draws 2217/2258 in-cluster, SNDR 70.09; DEVADD=1 bit-identical on T20/T81/T120 (max|d| 1.072e-04 / 2.258e-04 / 4.887e-04, SNDR 69.70/70.09/67.90) -- the device links never fire today, so the scaffold is provably inert. Instrumented audit (PT_V21_DEVDBG, to be reverted): rejection reasons at every Add -- 10 links fail with cons(out)=2 (the residual Add results have TWO consumers), the spine node 3866 fails with next_op=7 (PT_DIV, a host op), and all conv-site keeps fail so no operand is ever device-resident (devres a=0 b=0).
asi.hypothesis: Phase-5 flagship: the device-resident residual Add bundle (~121 MB/stream of copy traffic at the 22 big decoder Adds; run 88's marginal price 1.4 ms/MB => 30-90 ms). Scaffold: device add kernel with fused LeakyReLU epilogue, operand upload, host-sync fallback, chain eligibility, conv-site keep extension -- default OFF.
asi.learned: Scaffold is inert and safe (bit-exact with the flag ON), but the eligibility audit redefines the project: (1) the residual tree is a DAG -- Add results have 2 consumers, so cons==1 gates kill every link; a device tensor with several device-side readers is numerically fine, so the real requirement is LIVENESS, not consumer count; (2) the spine ends at a Div (host op), so the top of each tree must D2H anyway -- the traffic to win is the inner links; (3) the bump arena cannot serve multi-consumer lifetimes (a long-lived tensor blocks release of newer ones), so the project needs a device-arena free-list allocator with last-consumer release, plus a consumer LIST (not just the last consumer) to decide eligibility. Plan: consumer lists -> free-list allocator with refcount release -> relax eligibility to all-consumers-device-eligible. description: Winograd F(2,3) on the K=3 convs KILLED BY ARITHMETIC before spending a kernel: these are 1-D convolutions, where the 2-D transform amortization does not exist. Direct K=3 = 5 ops/output; Winograd F(2,3) 1-D = 3 input-transform adds + 2 mults + 3 output-transform adds = 8 ops/output (1.6x MORE work); F(4,3) ~9.5. The 2.25x figure is 2-D-only. asi.hypothesis: Phase-5 flagship candidate: Winograd F(2,3) on the K=3 convs (26 of them: 7x256->256, 6x192->768, 6x768->192, 6x128->128, 1x192->256), claimed by the backlog at 2.25x fewer multiplies / ~80-130 ms. Priced the arithmetic BEFORE writing a kernel.
asi.kill_arithmetic: Our convs are 1-D (time axis, channels are the GEMM dimension). Per output-channel-pair: direct K=3 = 3 mults + 2 adds = 5 ops. Winograd F(2,3) 1-D = input transform B^T (6 adds per 4-sample tile = 3/output) + 4 elementwise mults per tile = 2/output + output transform A^T (6 adds per 2 outputs = 3/output) = 8 ops/output, i.e. 1.6x MORE total ops than direct. The 2.25x figure is the 2-D number (9 mults -> 16/4): in 2-D the input transform amortizes across rows; in 1-D it does not. F(4,3) is worse still (tile 6, out 4: 1.5 mults + ~3 input-transform adds + ~5 output-transform adds = ~9.5 ops/output). On fp32 CUDA cores adds and multiplies cost the same, so a transform that trades 1 multiply for 3 adds is a loss, not a win.
asi.consequence: The last GPU-FLOP lever is closed by arithmetic. Remaining project-scale items (operator approval): batch-4 lockstep driver, CUDA graphs per stream, server-mode resident weights -- all launch/scheduling levers, not FLOP levers, with the run-87 measurement that the SMs are saturated during inference as the reason their ceiling is launch overhead (~1-2 ms), far below the bar.

description: Upload claim-order lever KILLED BY MECHANISM (no silicon): with one serialized copy engine, all bytes are queued at ~start and engine completion (~139 ms) is partition-invariant, so claim order cannot move the critical path. asi.kill_mechanism: No silicon spent. The Nano has ONE serialized copy path (~0.8 GB/s): with all four threads issuing their shares promptly, every byte is queued within microseconds of the start, so the engine finishes all 111 MB at ~139 ms regardless of which thread issued which copy. Claim order changes only issue order, not engine completion, and the startup barrier waits for engine completion -- so the critical path is the engine total, which is invariant under any partition. Run 77 already proved the engine rate is call-pattern-invariant (sync 138-141 ms == async 136-139 ms). Ceiling ~ a few ms: below the bar.
asi.other_plan_items: Ramp-burst size sweep: the adaptive gate's 8k maintenance burst costs ~3 ms at max clock, the full ramp ~26 ms; sweeping 2k/8k/16k can move at most ~2 ms (below bar, and shortening the burst weakens the worst-case thermal insurance of run 90). Record-pass fp32 memcpy skip for weight-only records (per-record host liveness): 84 MB memcpy at ~5 GB/s = ~17 ms serialized, ~5 ms/stream share once parallel = below bar, in the g_hcache refcount race zone. SNDR/close tail ~45 ms: run 296 measured that skipping the device frees makes it WORSE (+29 ms, lazy Tegra teardown); the SNDR compute itself is ~1 ms over 231k samples.

asi.kill_mechanism: Lockstep forces the 4 streams to align at every sync point, so each node costs max-over-streams instead of being statistically multiplexed. The streams are naturally desynchronized by 25-100 ms (run 106) and the run-87 trace shows the SMs are already saturated by cross-stream backfill: the packing gains batch-4 offers are exactly what natural desynchronization already harvests, while the sync cost is new. A sparse lockstep (only at the ~180 device launches) scales to ~180/4066 of the barrier cost only if the streams are already aligned at those points -- they are not (25-100 ms offsets), so each forced alignment burns the spread.

description: Templated-K window conv (PT_V21_WINK) KILLED at N=4: 2700 vs 2066 ms (4/4 pairs, +640 ms) even though the identical kernel is 1.9x FASTER than ig8 in the isolated bench (19.4 vs 36.7 ms, bit-exact). Mechanism: register-window loads are per-thread scalar (K+7 per channel), so the design is load-issue bound -- fine on an idle GPU with warm L1, fatal when 4 streams share 2 SMs

asi.bench_isolation: In the bench (one kernel, warm caches) a templated window kernel copies of the same code cost 19.4-20.8 ms vs 36.7-39.8 for the ig8-like direct_conv layout, bit-exact against a padded reference -- i.e. the bench says 1.9-2x FASTER.
asi.hypothesis: The window-direct conv's failure in run 317 was caused by the runtime K being a function argument, not a template parameter: `float xv[K+7]` indexed by a runtime k forces local-memory addressing, which is exactly why the variable-K version measured 39.8 ms in the bench while a `template<int TK>` copy measured 19.3 ms on identical math. If the same kernel is templated for K in {3,5,7,11}, the long-K convs (K=11 30% + K=7 21% + K=5 8% + K=3 15% of conv MACs) should run ~1.9x faster than ig8, cutting the conv total (427 ms/stream) by a large margin. Changed premise vs the run-317 kill: constant-K instantiation with zero spills (ptxas: 56 regs, 0 spill bytes for win<11>).
asi.mechanism: LOAD-ISSUE BOUND. Per input channel each thread issues K+7 predicated scalar global loads, and the 8 channel-threads of a time-group re-read the same window, so a block issues ~2300 loads per input channel against ig8's 2 float4 cooperative loads per chunk step. With warm L1 and an idle GPU (the single-kernel bench) that trade wins 2x on the FMA side; at N=4, where four streams share the 2 SMs, the extra load instructions contend for issue slots and the kernel collapses. This is the same lesson as the run-78 tail analysis: a single-stream kernel bench cannot predict the N=4 regime.
asi.numerics: SNDR 70.05 / 69.78 / 69.83 / 68.00 / 67.40 on the five golden cases (vs 70.09 / 69.70 / 69.93 / 67.90 / 67.45 with ig8): equal quality, different summation order. max|d| 2.087e-04 vs 2.258e-04. Bit-exactness was verified only in the bench (max|d| 0.000e+00 vs the padded reference).
asi.next_action_hint: Kernel-level levers are now closed from five directions (column tiling ig16, window-direct, FFT, Winograd arithmetic, batch-4 scheduling) -- stop trying to beat ig8. Pivot to GRAPH-LEVEL structure: run a dead-code/consumer analysis on the 4071-node graph to look for nodes whose outputs are never consumed (host-only work, zero risk), and to the last unexamined host op classes.

asi.rollback_reason: Implemented, bit-exactness-verified, and measured on both N=1 and N=4: ~1.5x slower per node in the runtime despite being 1.9x faster in the isolated bench, because the register-window design multiplies scalar load instructions per thread and the N=4 regime is issue-slot bound.

description: Clock-hold during the weight upload KILLED (6/6 pairs, +45 ms): the upload's 0.8 GB/s is the governor's ~600 ms SM-load ramp (clock trace 384->921 over 0.6 s), and no SM-side hold can buy it back. Micro-benchmarks also close coalescing (336 copies over 4 streams = 47.8 ms == one coalesced copy) and pinned/malloc source kinds (all 2.0-2.4 GB/s at max clock)

asi.clock_trace: Sampled cur_freq at 50 ms during a whole N=4 run: 768 (idle) -> 384 -> 691 -> 768 -> 844 -> 921, reaching max ~0.6 s after process start. The upload window (~100-350 ms) therefore runs at 384-768 MHz, i.e. 40-80% of max clock -- which is exactly the 0.8 GB/s vs the 2.4 GB/s the same copy achieves at max clock (measured in .auto/h2d_test4.cu: 336 records x 330 KB over 4 streams = 47.8 ms at max clock, 137 ms cold).
asi.hypothesis: The 111 MB weight upload runs at ~0.8 GB/s (139-170 ms) although the same copy reaches 2.4 GB/s (47 ms) when the GPU clock is at max -- because the copies are copy-engine work, which does not raise SM load, so the governor's ramp (driven by SM load) is not sustained past the short ramp kernel. Holding the clock for the whole upload with a long SM kernel (PT_V21_WARM_MS) should therefore convert ~90 ms of the startup into nothing: the kernel is joined after the upload, so it costs the critical path nothing.
asi.micro_benchmarks: Order-alternating best-of-3 H2D rates on the Nano: mmap+POPULATE 2.43 GB/s, mmap+HUGEPAGE 2.44, cudaMallocHost 2.14-3.18, malloc(pageable) 2.04-2.22 -- i.e. the host source kind does NOT matter (the earlier single-shot spread was the clock ramp, and cudaHostRegister on an anonymous mmap returns 'operation not supported'). Chunking overhead: 336 copies over 4 streams 47.8 ms vs one coalesced copy 47.4 ms at max clock, so per-copy overhead is negligible -- coalescing the upload is NOT a lever either.
asi.next_action_hint: The upload's 139-170 ms is clock-physics: it pays the governor's ~600 ms SM-load ramp, and no SM-side trick can buy that back without costing more than it saves. Startup is now closed with a mechanism (clock trace + copy-rate table), not just ceilings. Remaining loop work: cluster draws, both-box robustness, ledger/ideas upkeep.

Same family as run 284's overlap tie and run 90's shorter-ramp kill.

description: Zero-copy weight slab (cudaHostAlloc mapped + CPU fill, replacing the 139-170 ms H2D upload with 19-30 ms) KILLED: bit-exact and the upload does shrink, but the N=4 wall is +15 ms (5/6 pairs) -- the copies were paying for the governor's clock ramp, which now lands inside inference (+10 ms/stream of kernels)

asi.hypothesis: The 111 MB weight upload costs 139-170 ms of copy-engine time because it runs at the idle-clock rate (0.8 GB/s), while the SAME bytes can be filled by an ordinary CPU memcpy into a cudaHostAlloc(Mapped) buffer at 3.75 GB/s (31 ms) -- and on Tegra the GPU reads mapped host memory at device-memory rate, so the kernels can consume the slab in place. Replacing the H2D upload with a CPU fill of a mapped slab should therefore remove ~110-140 ms from the serialized startup.
asi.mechanism_finding: The copy path was inadvertently PAYING FOR THE CLOCK RAMP with otherwise-idle startup time. Removing the copy engine work removed the GPU activity that ramps the governor, so the ~600 ms ramp now lands inside the inference phase: N=1 CONV 435.7 vs 425.9 ms (+10 ms/stream of kernels at the lower clock) and the wall nets out to zero. This is the same clock physics that killed the SM-hold variant (run 331) from the other direction -- startup cannot be made shorter by removing GPU work, because the ramp needs GPU work somewhere and the startup is where it is cheapest.
asi.numerics: Bit-identical to the copy path on all 5 golden cases at N=1: max|d| 2.258e-04 / 1.072e-04 / 3.813e-04 / 4.887e-04 / 1.726e-04 and SNDR 70.09 / 69.70 / 69.93 / 67.90 / 67.45 in both arms. cudaHostGetDevicePointer returns the same address (unified addressing), cudaHostAlloc(Mapped) of 111 MB succeeds on picard, and the CPU fill into mapped memory runs at the same 3.75 GB/s as into anonymous memory (.auto/zcopy_test.cu).
asi.next_action_hint: Startup is closed from three directions now (SM-hold +45 ms, zero-copy slab ~0 net, coalescing/coalesced copies and source-kind pinning all within noise): the serialized 287 ms is bounded below by the governor's clock ramp. Loop: cluster draws, both-box robustness, ledger/ideas upkeep.

WARMLOG confirms the upload itself drops to 19-30 ms per stream (from 136-236). Reverted -- the mapped slab, the g_zcopy branches and PT_V21_ZCOPY are gone.

description: fp16 weight upload + in-kernel decode KILLED BY ARITHMETIC (no silicon; revived legitimately after run 287's assumption changed). Measured the container exactly: 339 records, raw 84.9 MiB vs expanded fp32 110.9 MiB; the 39 fp16 records (the decoder's packed *.wp#h conv/convT weights) are 26.0 MiB stored / 52.0 MiB expanded, so uploading as-stored saves exactly 26.0 MiB = 32.5 ms of copy-engine time (0.8 GB/s startup rate) and is BIT-EXACT (the host already decodes those records by LUT; __half2float yields identical bits). But the fused in-kernel decode costs fp16->fp32 converts in the staging loop of every decoder conv: 4 converts per staged float4 per thread per chunk against 128 FMAs, i.e. +3-12% of issue slots on ~1600 ms of conv+convT GPU work = +10-20 ms, against +1.6 ms of traffic saving. Net 0 to +20 ms on the wall for a change inside the run-#55 weight-cache/refcount zone across 6 kernel families (template<bool W16> doubles the instantiations). Closed by arithmetic, same standard as the phase-5 Winograd kill.

asi.hypothesis: Upload the 39 fp16 container records as stored (84.9 MiB not 110.9 MiB) and decode fp16->fp32 inside the kernels' weight-staging loop (no extra device pass, unlike run 287's split-half plan), converting 26 MiB of copy-engine time into ~0.

asi.kernel_price: ig8 stages Ws[16][16] float4 per block-chunk with 256 threads, so each thread stages 1 weight float4 = 4 weights per 128 FMAs. cvt.f32.f16 on Maxwell issues at a fraction of the FMA rate; at 1/4 rate that is 16 FMA slots = 12.5% of the FMA issue, at 1/2 rate 6%. On 1600 ms of conv+convT GPU time that is +10-20 ms -- the same order as the startup gain, with the traffic saving (+13 MiB of weight reads, ~1.6 ms at 8-12 GB/s) as a rounding term.

description: Kernel axis closed with THEORY (no silicon): ig8's inner loop is 3 LDS.128 loads per 32 FMAs per thread, and on this 1-SM part shared bandwidth is 128 B/clk, so a warp's 3 LDS.128 = 1536 B = 12 clocks against 8 clocks of FMA (1024 FMA / 128 lanes) -- the LDS pipe caps ig8 at 67% of FMA peak = 78.6 GFMA/s. Measured per-stream rate is 17.45 GFMA / 405 ms = 43 GFMA/s, i.e. 37% of the 118 GFMA/s hardware peak and 55% of the tile's LDS ceiling. The designs that raise the ceiling (80% at 1 w + 4 v = ig16) were measured WORSE (+10-31%, run 328) because their occupancy is lower -- so ig8 is at the practical optimum of a measured trade, and the whole kernel family is bounded at ~1.8x by shared-memory bandwidth, not by a bug.

asi.hypothesis: Quantify how far the shipped conv kernels are from the hardware ceiling of the 1-SM part, so the finalize report states the remaining upside as a number instead of a hope. Read the ig8 inner loop: per thread per rr, 1 Ws + 2 Xs float4 loads (3 LDS.128) and 32 FMAs (a[0..7] x 4).
asi.math: Maxwell shared bandwidth 128 B/clk/SM; a warp LDS.128 = 512 B = 4 clocks; 3 LDS.128 = 12 clocks; the same warp does 32 FMA x 32 threads = 1024 FMA = 8 clocks at 128 lanes -> LDS-bound, ceiling 8/12 = 67% of FMA peak = 78.6 GFMA/s (118 GFMA/s at 922 MHz, 1 SM x 128 lanes x 2 flop).
asi.measured: per-stream GPU 34.9 GFLOP = 17.45 GFMA (run 71) in 401.7 ms kernel+sync (run 350 profile) = 43 GFMA/s = 36% of hardware peak = 55% of the tile's LDS ceiling; the residual 45% is barrier + global staging per 16-rr chunk, the 8.5% tail-wave waste (run 78) and 4-stream congestion on 4 resident block slots.
asi.ceiling_trade_bracket: the 80%-ceiling shape (1 w + 4 v = 64 FMA per 5 LDS.128) is exactly ig16, measured +10-31% in the kernel bench (run 328) because Xs[16][64] = 16 KB drops blocks/SM; the 16-accumulator shape (4 output columns per thread) measured 39% slower (phase 1); -maxrregcount 48/56 lost. So no shape in the family beats ig8 at this occupancy, which the occupancy probe (run 348: ig8 = 4 blocks/SM, register-limited) now explains quantitatively.
asi.report_line: conv kernels are at 37% of the 1-SM fp32 peak and 55% of their own tile's LDS-bandwidth ceiling; the theoretical headroom is 1.8x and every structural route to it is measured-worse (occupancy), so a >20% kernel win requires a different algorithm, and FFT (10x slower), Winograd 1-D (1.6x more ops) and register-window (+640 ms at N=4) are the measured answers to that request.

description: Kernel micro-bench pair (.auto/ig8_bench.cu ablation + .auto/ig8_v2_bench.cu candidates, standalone, no runtime change): the shipped ig8 tile in ISOLATION runs 43-69 GFMA/s while the runtime measures its nodes at 18-23 GFMA/s, so the tile is NOT the 3x gap -- the gap is the per-node wrapper (host zero-pad memcpy + H2D/D2H staging) plus the mid-run clock (~700 of 921 MHz). Ablation of the tile: removing per-chunk X staging +45%, W staging +49%, barriers +64%, and HALVING FMA-per-LDS made it FASTER (+72%), so the tile is staging/barrier-latency bound, NOT LDS-bandwidth bound (my run-352 ceiling theory is falsified by measurement). Candidate fixes measured: register-pipelined staging (loads issued before compute) = +9% on the biggest node, -2..-3% on the other three; RK=32 chunks (half the barriers) = -16..-26%. No integration proposed: the staging cost belongs to device residency, which is closed by measurement at +261 ms (run 305).

asi.hypothesis: The per-node efficiency table showed every dominant conv at 21.6-24.3 GFMA/s (19% of the 1-SM 118 GFMA/s peak), so locate the 3-5x gap by ablation instead of guessing: clone the shipped tile in a bench, remove one term at a time, then measure the candidate fixes (chunk width RK, software-pipelined staging).
asi.ablation_table_shape1: A exact clone 43.2 GFMA/s | B X staged once 62.7 | C half the X staging 74.3 | D no barriers 70.7 | E W staged once 64.5 (B-E are timing-only ablations)
asi.tile_is_not_the_gap: isolated clone 43-69 GFMA/s vs runtime node rate 18-23 -- a 2.5-3x difference that cannot be the tile (identical structure). Decomposition: (a) the clock during inference is 384-921 MHz on a ramp, ~700 MHz average => 1.3x; (b) the runtime's per-node time includes the host zero-pad scratch memcpy and the H2D/D2H staging of that node's input/output (run 88 measured copies at ~1.4 ms/MB, 20-30% exposed), which is exactly the staging the ablation shows is the tile's biggest cost; (c) wave tails (8.5% MAC-weighted, run 78).
asi.consequence: the only lever that addresses the dominant term (per-node staging traffic) is device residency, which is closed by measurement (+261 ms at N=4, run 305) because the added device passes cost SM time on a saturated 1-SM part. Kernel-tile work is closed from 8 directions now (column tiling, window-direct, templated-K, FFT, Winograd, block count, occupancy/carveout, chunk-width/pipelining).
asi.bench_caveat: the bench's own numerics are unresolved (max|d| 1.58e18 vs a naive reference in the v2 family; the pad_in>=0 clone mismatched too), so its ABSOLUTE rates are indicative only -- used for relative ablation at fixed structure, and no code was integrated. Kept as artifacts: .auto/ig8_bench.cu, .auto/ig8_v2_bench.cu, .auto/occ_probe.cu.
asi.lesson: BENCHMARK LESSON #3: a kernel's isolated rate can be 2.5-3x better than the same kernel's rate in the runtime; the difference is the wrapper (pad-scratch memcpy + staging copies) and the clock ramp, not the tile. Never quote a bench GFMA/s as an achievable runtime rate.

description: Single-stream occupancy probe (no code change; N4=1 official, 1 pair): forcing the 64-column conv kernel (PT_V21_IG8_MINT=4096, 5 blocks/SM = 62.5% occupancy) gives N=1 wall 1234 ms / stream 641 ms vs the shipped ig8 (4 blocks/SM = 50% occupancy) 1252 / 649 -- a tie (-18 ms wall, -8 ms stream, 1 pair).
